validity.population: nine healthy adults from Harms et al. 2003 mapped to the schematic BVS95 graph
validity.physiological_state: sustained 70-degree head-up tilt; global-flow sensitivity profile
validity.description: Cardiac output is scaled from the reported median 6.0 L/min supine to 4.7 L/min during sustained head-up tilt. Posture-dependent cerebral venous rerouting is not represented by BVS95.

sources.citation: Harms MPM et al. Postural effects on cardiac output and mixed venous oxygen saturation in humans. Exp Physiol. 2003;88:611-616. doi:10.1113/eph8802580.

sources.citation: Gisolf J et al. Human cerebral venous outflow pathway depends on posture and central venous pressure. J Physiol. 2004;560:317-327. doi:10.1113/jphysiol.2004.070409.
sources.license: Citation and qualitative model limitation only; article rights remain with the publisher.

limitations: This is a global-flow sensitivity scenario, not a complete orthostatic circulation model.
BVS95 lacks the vertebral venous plexus that becomes a major cerebral outflow pathway upright; therefore no jugular transition override is scientifically justified.
The source cohort is small and the reported cardiac-output range shows substantial inter-individual variation.
Pressure, venous collapse, baroreflexes and time-dependent orthostatic adaptation are absent.
